title-1.purpose: Page titles and auth titles. Shrinks to 1.75rem on 2rem below 760 px.

title-2.purpose: Drop zone title, empty states, import result and error titles, the small-screen editor message, landing step numbers.

heading.purpose: Dialog, sheet and card titles, site names on the dashboard, landing step titles.

title-3.purpose: The site name in the editor top bar.

lead.purpose: The sentence under a page title or the landing headline, in ink 2.

body.purpose: Sentences and input text. The reading measure is 66ch (`--measure`).

control.purpose: Buttons, nav rows, menu items, alerts, toasts.

label.purpose: Field labels and sidebar group titles.

meta.purpose: Timestamps, hints, counts, tooltips, in ink 3 or ink 2.

micro.purpose: Pills, keyboard hints, DNS record types, and the selection slug (`--kind-label-size`). Table column heads use micro in uppercase at 0.04em.

brand.purpose: The Pagehaven wordmark beside the flat ink logo.

mono.purpose: DNS values and file paths only.

shadows.name: focus-ring
shadows.purpose: Keyboard focus on every control: a surface gap and a Proof Cyan band. Pair with outline: 2px solid transparent for forced colors.

shadows.name: shadow-float
shadows.purpose: Menus, popovers, the floating toolbar and toasts. Always with border-float.

shadows.name: shadow-dialog
shadows.purpose: Dialogs and sheets, over the scrim. Always with an ink edge.

shadows.name: shadow-canvas
shadows.purpose: Keyline around the editor canvas frame on the sunken backdrop.

shadows.name: border-float
shadows.purpose: The ink edge on every floating thing.

shadows.name: device-bezel
shadows.purpose: Phone preview frame around the canvas (with a 38px radius).

motion.name: dur-fast
motion.purpose: Hover, press and color changes; the floating toolbar.

motion.name: dur-pop
motion.purpose: Menus, tooltips, toasts, the selection glide, sidebar chevrons.

motion.name: dur-device
motion.purpose: Computer and phone width change of the canvas.

motion.name: ease-in-out
motion.purpose: Looping motion such as the indeterminate progress bar.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: All durations under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce; state changes stay instant.

overlay.name: overlay-chip-bg
overlay.purpose: Fill of the slug that names the part.

overlay.name: overlay-veil
overlay.purpose: Stripe over parts that cannot be edited.

overlay.name: crop-mark
overlay.purpose: Arm length of each crop mark.

overlay.name: crop-gap
overlay.purpose: Crop marks sit this far outside the corner.

overlay.name: crop-weight
overlay.purpose: Crop mark stroke on screens (.crop); .crop-select uses select-stroke in Proof Cyan.

overlay.name: kind-label-size
overlay.purpose: Type size of the slug: Heading, Image.

overlay.name: device-radius
overlay.purpose: The phone screen corner inside its bezel; a depicted device outside the radius scale.

overlay.name: veil
overlay.purpose: Sheet white veil over the old page while it reloads.

layout.name: control-h-lg
layout.purpose: Also every target under pointer: coarse.

layout.name: dialog-w-wide
layout.purpose: Website settings, where the DNS table needs room.

layers.name: z-menu-over-toolbar

narrative.overview:
Pagehaven's chrome is the printer's proof an owner checks before their words go out. It is black ink on plain near-white stock, cut with hairline rules, and nothing else. The interface has no hue of its own, so the owner's website is the only color on screen. Confidence comes from contrast and precision, not from color, size or decoration.

One bright thing exists: Proof Cyan, the color of a press check. It means what you are touching right now, where keyboard focus is, and where a link goes. Selection on the canvas is a cyan rule with crop marks outside the corners and a filled slug that names the part ("Heading", "Image"). The overlay tokens for that are defined now; the overlay itself lands in a later phase.

Density is calm and legible. Text starts at 15 px for sentences, controls are 36 px tall and grow to 44 px under touch. Motion is mechanical and short and never bounces. Surfaces are flat. Only things that float above the page lift, and they carry a 1 px ink edge so they read as a sheet laid on top.
keyCharacteristics: Ink on warm near-white, no brand hue in the chrome.
Proof Cyan only for selection, focus and links.
One solid ink primary button per view.
Hairline rules separate regions; shadows only on floating things.
Small, sharp radii from 2 px to 8 px.
Schibsted Grotesk for the interface; Newsreader 450 for display titles outside the editor.
Lucide line icons at about 1.5 px rendered stroke.

rules.name: The No Hue Rule
rules.body: The chrome has no color of its own. Hue appears only in the select tokens, the link tokens and the state colors.

rules.name: The One Cyan Rule
rules.body: Proof Cyan means selection, focus or link. Never use it for decoration, headings, icons at rest or the primary button.

rules.name: The Word First Rule
rules.body: A state color always comes with a word or a shape. "Saved", "Published" and "Changes not published" carry the meaning; the dot only confirms it.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: Schibsted Grotesk sets every interface role. Newsreader 450 sets only display titles outside the editor: the landing headline, page and auth titles, the drop zone title, empty states, import result and error titles, and the small-screen editor message.

rules.name: The Quiet Editor Rule
rules.body: Never use Newsreader in editor chrome. The owner's site supplies the editor's personality.

rules.name: The Digit Column Rule
rules.body: Tabular numerals only on digit-only columns (`.tnum`, numeric table cells). Schibsted's tabular figures space commas and words oddly, so never set them on running text.

rules.name: The System Mono Rule
rules.body: There is no mono web font. The system ui-monospace stack shows DNS values and paths, nothing else.

rules.name: The Float Only Rule
rules.body: No decorative shadows. A shadow means the thing floats, and a floating thing always has a 1 px ink edge.

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: Separate regions with a 1 px rule, not with shadow, tint or space alone.

rules.name: The Small Radius Rule
rules.body: Radii stay on the 2, 3, 4, 6 and 8 px steps. Pill shapes are only for dots, the avatar, the switch and progress.

dos: Do keep the chrome ink, stock and hairline. Let the owner's site be the only color.
Do use exactly one ink primary button per view.
Do save Proof Cyan for selection, focus and links.
Do pair every state color with a word or a shape.
Do separate regions with 1 px hairlines and use ink rules only where the rule carries meaning.
Do give every floating thing a 1 px ink edge and the float or dialog shadow.
Do set every interface role in Schibsted Grotesk.
Do use Newsreader 450 only for display titles outside the editor.
Do use tabular numerals only on digit-only columns.
Do take icons from the Lucide sprite at 16, 20 or 24 px, and give every icon-only button an aria-label.
Do keep every target at 44 px under touch.
donts: Don't add a brand hue, tint or gradient to the chrome.
Don't use Proof Cyan for decoration, headings or the primary button.
Don't put a shadow on a card, panel, sidebar or button.
Don't use Newsreader in editor chrome.
Don't load a mono web font.
Don't set tabular numerals on text with commas or words.
Don't draw an icon by hand or use a text glyph as an icon.
Don't round past 8 px except for dots, the avatar, the switch and progress.
Don't let color alone carry a status.
